title: Desórdenes informativos y polarización afectiva: un análisis de las emociones en publicaciones con desinformación en tres conflictos políticos brasileños en Twitter / Information disorders and affective polarization: an analysis of emotions in posts with disinformation in three Brazilian political conflicts on Twitter
screen_reason: Qualitative content analysis of the 100 most-retweeted tweets from each of three Brazilian Twitter conflicts (n = 300): abortion decriminalisation (15-16 April 2020), the killing of João Alberto Freitas at a Carrefour store (20-21 November 2020) and the Supreme Court's establishment of the Covid-19 parliamentary inquiry (9-10 April 2021). Two human coders classified each tweet for presence and type of information disorder using Wardle and Derakhshan's typology, verifying claims against traditional news portals. Table 4 gives counts by type and per conflict, and the text states that 95 of the 300 posts carried some information disorder - a CONTENT share of items with an explicit denominator.

estimates.date: Three 24-hour collection windows: 15-16 April 2020 (abortion decriminalisation), 20-21 November 2020 (João Alberto / Carrefour racism case), 9-10 April 2021 (Covid-19 CPI)
estimates.measure_type: % of the 100 most-retweeted tweets in each of three Brazilian political conflicts (pooled) that were coded as containing some type of information disorder
estimates.value_raw: 95/300 = 31.7% ('casi un tercio de las publicaciones de la muestra presentan algún tipo de trastorno de la información (95 en total)'); Table 4: no mis/disinformation 140, suspended account 65, so 95 coded with a disorder
estimates.denominator: 300 tweets: the 100 most-retweeted tweets from each of three keyword-collected conflict corpora (91,251 tweets on abortion; 429,863 on the racism case; 623,537 on the Covid CPI)
estimates.definition: Tweet coded as containing at least one of Wardle and Derakhshan's information-disorder types - satire or parody, misleading content, imposter content, fabricated content, false connection, false context, manipulated content - after checking the claim against traditional news portals
estimates.misinfo_def: The paper works from Wardle and Derakhshan's (2018) information-disorder typology; operationally, “se analizaron todos los mensajes de las publicaciones analizadas, ya sea texto, imagen o video, y se verificó en portales de noticias tradicionales la veracidad de la información presentada” [all the messages analysed were examined, whether text, image or video, and the veracity of the information presented was checked against traditional news portals].
estimates.source_quote: Profundizando en los datos de esta tabla, se constata que cuando se observan los tres conflictos juntos, casi un tercio de las publicaciones de la muestra presentan algún tipo de trastorno de la información (95 en total). [Going deeper into the data in this table, it is found that when the three conflicts are observed together, almost a third of the posts in the sample present some type of information disorder (95 in total).]
estimates.page_loc: Section 4.2 Tipos de desinformación, p. 79; Table 4
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two human coders applied the Wardle and Derakhshan typology; the authors state they followed Sampaio and Lycarião's procedure for category testing and an inter-coder reliability test - but NO reliability statistic (kappa, alpha or percent agreement) is reported anywhere. Veracity was checked against traditional Brazilian news portals rather than fact-check ratings. Some tweets received a double classification, so the type counts (118) exceed the number of tweets with a disorder (95).
estimates.moderator_quote: Se investigaron los 100 tuits más influyentes de cada uno mediante un análisis cualitativo de contenido. Estos 100 tuits más retuiteados representan los mensajes con mayor alcance y visibilidad, totalizando un alcance de 300 tuits analizados en total.
estimates.notes: Three things a user of this number must know. (1) BROAD DEFINITION: 'information disorder' here includes satire or parody (17 tweets) and 'misleading content' (63 tweets), which the authors describe as 'critical arguments that do not provide a fact but the user's opinion as if it were the truth'. Much of the numerator is therefore opinion and irony, not false factual claims - hence breadth=misleading and borderline=true. (2) UNCODABLE TWEETS IN THE DENOMINATOR: 65 of the 300 tweets (21.7%) could not be retrieved because the post was deleted or the account suspended, and they are counted in the denominator as if they carried no disorder. 31.7% is therefore a LOWER bound; the authors explicitly note these posts probably run in the same direction as the disinformation cases. Computing 95/235 = 40.4% on assessable tweets only would be a value the paper never states, so it is not recorded. (3) CURATED DENOMINATOR: these are the 100 MOST RETWEETED tweets per conflict, not a random sample, so the figure describes the most visible content in a conflict spike, not the prevalence of disinformation on Brazilian Twitter. Year coded 2020 because two of the three collection windows fall in 2020; the Covid CPI window is April 2021.

estimates.date: Three 24-hour collection windows: 15-16 April 2020, 20-21 November 2020, 9-10 April 2021
estimates.measure_type: % of the 300 most-retweeted tweets across three Brazilian political conflicts coded as FABRICATED content (wholly false information)
estimates.value_raw: 15/300 = 5.0% fabricated content (Aborto 3, Racismo 0, CPI 12 = 15 total); '15 de ellos tenían contenido fabricado (tabla 4), es decir, información 100% falsa'
estimates.denominator: The same 300 most-retweeted tweets (100 per conflict)
estimates.definition: Tweet classified as 'fabricated content' in the Wardle and Derakhshan typology, which the authors gloss as 'información 100% falsa' (100% false information)
estimates.misinfo_def: Wardle and Derakhshan (2018) information-disorder typology; fabricated content glossed by the authors as wholly false information.
estimates.source_quote: 18 tweets tenían en su redacción una conexión falsa entre los puntos mencionados, 17 de ellos tenían información falsa con el objetivo de satirizar la situación y 15 de ellos tenían contenido fabricado (tabla 4), es decir, información 100% falsa.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Same two-coder qualitative classification against traditional news portals; no reliability statistic reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: Fabricated content — Aborto 3, Caso de Racismo 0, Establecimiento de la CPI 12, Total 15 [Tabla 4]
estimates.notes: STRICT-VERACITY variant of the row above, and the more useful one for a prevalence synthesis: it isolates wholly false content (5.0%) from the broad 31.7% that includes satire and opinion-as-fact. Because tweets could receive more than one disorder label, some of these 15 also carry another type, so this is not a clean partition of the 95. The same 65 unretrievable tweets sit in the denominator, so this too is a lower bound.

missed_or_uncertain: NOT extracted, with reasons. (a) PER-CONFLICT shares. Only one of the three is stated verbatim - 'el conflicto con más desórdenes informativos (40 tuits de la muestra)' for the Covid CPI case, i.e. 40/100 = 40%. The other two (abortion 30/100, racism 25/100) exist only as complements of Table 4's 'no disinformation' and 'suspended account' rows, and R8 bars computed complements and cross-category sums. Extracting only the CPI case would put the highest-disorder conflict into the dataset with the other two missing, which would bias any topic-level analysis, so the pooled figure is used instead and the CPI number is recorded here for the record. (b) Individual disorder-type counts other than fabricated content (misleading content 63, false connection 18, satire/parody 17, imposter 2, manipulated 2, false context 1) - kept out because double-coding makes them non-exclusive and because satire/parody and 'opinion stated as truth' are not veracity categories the review should pool; the two rows extracted bracket the range (5.0% strict, 31.7% broad). (c) Table 5 emotion classifications and the emotion-disinformation association - not prevalence. (d) The raw conflict volumes in Table 3 (91,251 / 429,863 / 623,537 tweets) - corpus sizes, not misinformation shares; note Table 3's abortion row repeats 71,766 in both the retweet and total columns, which contradicts the 91,251 given in the text, and the CPI total is 623,479 in the table versus 623,537 in the text. (e) The 65 deleted/suspended posts are reported as a count only and cannot be classified; they are a known and unquantifiable downward bias on both extracted values.

rob.design: Twitter streaming-API keyword collection for three Brazilian online conflicts, each over a 24-hour window (abortion 15-16 April 2020; João Alberto/Carrefour racism case 20-21 November 2020; Covid-19 CPI 9-10 April 2021), producing corpora of roughly 91k, 430k and 624k tweets. From each, the 100 most-retweeted tweets were taken for qualitative content analysis (n = 300) - a rank-truncated, popularity-selected sample. Two human coders classified presence and type of information disorder per Wardle and Derakhshan (2018), checking veracity against traditional news portals; an inter-coder reliability test is said to have been run following Sampaio and Lycarião (2021) but no statistic is given. 65 of the 300 tweets (21.7%) were unretrievable (deleted posts or suspended accounts) and could not be coded, yet remain in the denominator. Tweets could receive more than one disorder label. No confidence intervals; no sensitivity analysis.
rob.item6_quote: El primero tiene como objetivo realizar una investigación sobre la presencia o ausencia de mis o desinformación ... realizando en los casos positivos, la clasificación de los mismos, según la literatura de Wardle y Derakhshan (2018) ... Para eso, se analizaron todos los mensajes de las publicaciones analizadas, ya sea texto, imagen o video, y se verificó en portales de noticias tradicionales la veracidad de la información presentada.
